title: Trouble on the road
persona: You are a talkative Sydney taxi driver. You are friendly but a bit careless: you forget to start the meter and like taking the 'scenic route'. You use Australian expressions and speak quickly.
briefTr: Sidney Havalimanı'ndan Harbour Hotel'e taksiyle gideceksin. Taksimetrenin açık olduğundan, en kısa yoldan gidildiğinden emin ol. Otelin önünde inmek istiyorsun.

facts.question: How much was the bridge toll?

goals.titleTr: Nereye gideceğini ve sabit fiyatı sormak
goals.instruction: The passenger says where to go and asks if there is a fixed price.
goals.hint: To the Harbour Hotel, please. Is there a fixed price?
goals.hintTr: Harbour Hotel'e, lütfen. Sabit fiyat var mı?
goals.successReply: No fixed price, mate — it's on the meter.

goals.instruction: The meter is not on. The passenger politely asks the driver to turn it on.
goals.hint: Could you turn on the meter, please?
goals.successReply: Oh, whoops! Sorry, mate. It's on now.

goals.ask: I'll take you the scenic route — you'll love the view!
goals.instruction: The driver suggests a longer, 'scenic' route. The passenger asks for the fastest or shortest way.
goals.hint: Can we take the shortest way, please?
goals.hintTr: En kısa yoldan gidebilir miyiz, lütfen?
goals.successReply: Fair enough, the quick way it is.
goals.retryReply: Is the scenic route okay with you, or are you in a hurry?

goals.ask: We'll go over the Harbour Bridge.
goals.instruction: The passenger asks about the toll or extra charges for the bridge.
goals.hint: Is there a toll on the bridge?
goals.successReply: Yeah, it's {toll}. It goes on the fare.

goals.ask: Here's the hotel. Front or side entrance?
goals.instruction: The passenger asks the driver to stop at the right place, for example the hotel entrance.
goals.hint: Can you pull over here, please?
goals.retryReply: Where would you like me to drop you?

goals.instruction: The passenger pays and asks for a receipt.
goals.hint: By card, please. And a receipt.
goals.retryReply: How would you like to pay?

twists.intro: Oops — I think I missed the turn.
twists.instruction: The driver took a wrong turn. The passenger asks to turn around, asks if it will cost more, or asks to use the map.
twists.retryReply: Sorry about that. Give me a sec.

options.text: Will it cost more because of this?
options.reply: No, I'll take ten dollars off. My mistake.

options.text: Can we use the map on my phone?
options.reply: Good idea, I'll follow your map.

twists.intro: Road's closed ahead — we'll have to take a detour.
twists.instruction: A road is closed. The passenger asks how long it adds, asks for another way, or says it's fine.
twists.retryReply: Nothing I can do about that one!

options.text: How much longer will it take?

options.reply: I'll go around through the city, should be quick.
Good on ya. Won't be long.

twists.intro: Mind if I take a quick phone call?
twists.instruction: The driver wants to talk on the phone while driving. The passenger politely says no, agrees if hands-free, or asks to keep it short.

options.reply: Fair enough, I'll call her back.

options.text: Okay, but please keep it short.

twists.instruction: The card did not work. The passenger asks to try again, offers another card, or offers cash.
twists.retryReply: Happens all the time. Got another way to pay?

options.reply: Let's see… yep, went through this time.
Sure, tap it here… all good.

twists.intro: I haven't got change for a hundred, sorry.
twists.instruction: The driver has no change. The passenger offers a card, asks to stop at a shop, or asks the hotel to break the note.

options.text: Can we stop at a shop for change?
options.reply: There's one right here, no worries.

options.text: I'll ask the hotel reception for change.

twists.intro: Just so you know, there's a five percent surcharge for cards.
twists.instruction: There is a card surcharge. The passenger accepts, pays cash instead, or asks why.
twists.retryReply: That's the rule in Sydney cabs.

options.text: That's fine, I'll still pay by card.

options.reply: The card companies charge us, so we pass it on. Sorry!

closing: Cheers, mate. Have a ripper of a trip!
